senate_gov.name: U.S. Senate, Party Division
senate_gov.licence: a publication of the U.S. Senate; no licence printed

chamber.rule: 51 of 100 seats, or 50 with the Vice President's vote; seats not up and independents counted by caucus

vice_president.note: the model's own chance that the Democrat wins the College, from its forecast on 538's national average of 2012-11-05 (the presidency's p in data/president/2012.json stands under the model's own): states whole, a 269 tie counted half; assumed independent of the Senate's common swing

chamber.seat_model: y_i = mean_i + swing_loading_i * d + e_i, d ~ N(0, common_swing_sd^2), e_i ~ N(0, own_sd_i^2), each seat's stage_two.inputs giving mean, own_sd, swing_loading
chamber.not_up_source: the winner of each seat's latest election before 2012: Cha, Kuriwaki and Snyder from 2006, MEDSL's U.S. Senate 1976-2024 before

notes: 1. Jeffrey Chiesa (R) of New Jersey, appointed June 6, 2013, was seated, replacing Frank Lautenberg (D), who died on June 3, 2013.
2. Cory Booker (D) of New Jersey, elected October 16, 2013, was seated, replacing appointed Senator Jeffrey Chiesa (R).

model.what: the model's own forecast (data/congress/REPORT.md section 2), fitted on earlier cycles only, from what was known before the election (the orchestrator, 2026-11-07 05:58); no polls are used, so it carries less than forecasters then knew

calibration.note: k = the root mean square of z = (y - mean) / sd over these earlier years' races, each year forecast from its own earlier cycles

model.sd_is: sqrt(national_sd^2 + s_e^2); national_sd = k s_a sqrt(1 + z (Z'Z)^-1 z'), s_e = k s_e_fitted, z = (1, midterm * P, (1 - midterm) * P), P = +1 Democratic president, -1 Republican; k the calibration factor

fte_538.version_note: 538 showed one version by default; no source read here names it, so the version listed first in its repository's rows comes first and the others stand beside it (the orchestrator, 04:12)

notes: A candidate is endorsed by the party at the party convention.
